title: Ultimately Flat After Options-Driven Volatility
summary:
Ultimately Flat After Options-Driven Volatility 

             
             
            Treasuries continued in the same sideways holding pattern seen over the past 4 trading sessions. This generally mirrors a holding pattern in certain tech companies' credit risk metrics. In short, bonds currently have nothing better to do than wait and see if tech is experiencing some kind of true inflection point or just a false alarm. Today was set to be especially boring as a result, but there was some afternoon volatility surrounding the options expiration cut-off (which affected both Treasuries and stocks). Even then, the net effect of that volatility was less than 1.5bps of weakness in 10yr yields (5.124 after the dust settled versus 5.112 before the spike).

title: Mortgage Rates End Flat After Starting Slightly Lower
summary: It was another ho-hum day for mortgage rates, which is more of the exception than the rule these days. But we're not complaining! The uneventful, sideways movement means rates are holding in line with the lowest levels in nearly a month.  Today would have been slightly lower than yesterday had it not been for some mid-day weakness in the underlying bond market. While there were a few war-related headlines that coincided with the timing, the volatility is more attributable to esoteric trader positioning considerations in the Treasury options market.

title: Fulfillment, Home Price Performance, Borrower Assistance Tools; Webinars; Non-Agency Products
summary: Let’s see what’s in my electronic mailbag. “Rob, is it true that LOs can now join the MBA directly?” Yup. There’s MBA Homebase that provides loan officers with education, coaching, professional development, and a stronger voice in the mortgage industry. It is open to loan officers at every lender and across every origination channel, regardless of whether their company is an MBA member. “Rob, I watched President Trump talk about Montana being helped, financially, by Fannie and Freddie. Is that legal?” Hah, define “legal.” Montana has about 10,000 sales a year, $3 billion divided by 10,000 is $300,000. He is just saying that Fannie and Freddie are going to keep doing what they always have done: facilitate home loans? Or will Bill Pulte have state-based loan level price adjustments, which some may view as politically based? Stay tuned. “Rob, since Clinton and Congress last balanced the budget, we’ve had a deficit. Why do we care now?” First off, it’s a huge, unimaginable number, and no politician even wants to talk about it. Let’s face it: we’re spending money that we don’t have. The U.S. government, with its $40 trillion in debt, isn't the only one with a debt problem. 1 in 5 Americans fell behind on a loan or mortgage payment in 2025, according to new data from the Federal Reserve. That figure is up from 1 in 8 Americans in 2022 and marks the highest level since 2007. Why is it happening, and what will it mean for the economy? (Today’s podcast can be found here. This week’s ‘casts are presented by Experian. Experian Verify’s integration with Workday gives mortgage lenders broader access to reliable, up-to-date income and employment data, streamlining verification, enhancing efficiency, and delivering a smoother borrower experience from application to closing. Today’s has an interview with Knock’s Sean Black on the company’s buy-before-you-sell program, which allows homeowners to access their existing home equity to purchase a new home before selling their current one.)

title: Waiting For Whatever's Next
summary: We find ourselves in a bit of a lull in the bond market this week, and we don't object! Yields aren't screaming back up toward recent highs. Nor are they extending last week's swift rally. Both would cause problems for different reasons. Consolidating last week's rally in this narrow, sideways pattern is arguably the very best thing that could have happened this week. Whatever happens next is likely to be driven by a combination of the evolving narrative on tech sector concerns, econ data, and the Fed policy stance (which is really just a function of the econ data). In general, it is the tech sector narrative that has kept us in this week's lull. There too, investors are waiting for whatever's next.

UWM Waives FHA And VA Credit-Score Pricing Hits Through Year-End
summary: United Wholesale Mortgage is waiving credit-score-based loan-level pricing adjustments on FHA and VA loans for borrowers with scores of 580 or higher, giving brokers a reason to revisit eligible quotes where credit-based costs have been an obstacle.The wholesale lender also reduced its pricing adjustment on VA cash-out refinances above 90% loan-to-value from 1.250 to 0.750. Both changes apply to locks through Dec. 31.

title: The Non-QM Opportunity Beyond The Rate Conversation
summary: I’ve been on the road a lot recently, talking with originators about where they’re finding business. Rates come up in almost every conversation. But when I ask what’s actually closing, I keep hearing the same thing: many of the originators doing well have made non-agency lending a meaningful part of their business.These conversations aren’t a market study, but the pattern has my attention. Business is still getting done. Some originators have found borrowers who are willing and able to move, even with today’s high-rate environment.

title: Second Baltimore Mortgage Fraud Suit Details Foreclosure Fallout
summary: A second federal lawsuit involving several of the investors and appraisers named in AmeriTrust Mortgage Corp.’s Baltimore fraud case alleges another 59 loans defaulted, leaving two lenders pursuing foreclosures and taking ownership of properties they claim were materially overvalued.

title: Servicer Takes New York Payment-Fee Fight To Federal Court
summary: Onity Group, the parent of mortgage servicer Onity Mortgage, has taken a dispute over optional expedited-payment fees to federal court, arguing that New York has not adequately explained how servicers should determine whether those charges meet the state’s cost standard.The company said it filed a declaratory judgment action Oct. 20 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of New York. In a same-day SEC filing, Onity disclosed that regulators have requested information about its optional-payment fee practices and that discussions with New York regulators are ongoing.

title: January’s Condo Reserve Increase Puts Project Budgets In Focus
summary: With a higher condo reserve requirement taking effect Jan. 4, loan originators preparing for early-2027 business should bring association budgets into the financing conversation now. A project that supported an earlier closing may need another look before the next buyer applies.Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac announced the increase in March, raising the minimum annual replacement-reserve allocation from 10% to 15% under applicable project reviews. Originators should work with their project-review teams to determine whether an association’s budget supports financing under the new requirements or another available review pathway.

title: Fairway Welcomes Back Gilmore, Gray, And Their 28-Member Team
summary: An underwriting decision, a looming closing deadline, or a problem requiring executive attention can put a lender’s support into focus. For Jeff Gilmore and Matt Gray, two years away reinforced its value.The regional managers returned to Fairway Home Mortgage in September with their 28-member Fairway Custom Mortgage team, based in Matthews, North Carolina, the lender announced Oct. 20. The managers had spent two years at Novus Home Mortgage after the group’s 2010–2024 tenure at Fairway.Fairway attributed $250 million in loan production to the returning team.

title: UWM Targets The 20%-Down Myth In New Push For Brokers
summary: United Wholesale Mortgage is taking a familiar LO conversation to a national audience: borrowers have more financing options than a 30-year mortgage with 20% down.“The wholesale lender announced Oct. 20 that its consumer-facing Mortgage Matchup brand is launching a new commercial encouraging homebuyers and homeowners to explore those options with a local independent mortgage broker.”The campaign will run nationwide across television, streaming, digital, and social media platforms.
